ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
(2016 · Hubei Huanggang Key Middle School senior three monthly exam) As shown in the figure, between the two plates of a parallel-plate capacitor there is a charged small ball (which may be regarded as a particle). When the charge quantity of the capacitor is Q1 (plate A is positively charged), the small ball is just stationary at point P. When the charge quantity of the capacitor suddenly increases to Q2, the charged small ball begins to move upward. After time t, make plate A negatively charged and plate B positively charged, and the charge quantity is still Q2; then after another time t the charged small ball just returns to point P. Neglect all resistance, and the small ball does not collide with the plates during its motion. Then (　　)
A.Q2＝2Q1 
B.Q2＝3Q1 
C.Q2＝4Q1 
D.Q2＝5Q1

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, between the two plates of a parallel-plate capacitor there is a charged small ball (which may be regarded as a particle). When the charge quantity of the capacitor is Q1 (plate A is positively charged), the small ball is just stationary at point P; when the charge quantity of the capacitor suddenly increases to Q2, the charged small ball begins to move upward. After time t, make plate A negatively charged and plate B positively charged, and the charge quantity is still Q2; then after another time t the charged small ball just returns to point P. Neglect all resistance, and the small ball does not collide with the plates during its motion. Ask: what relation do Q2 and Q1 satisfy?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there are two upper and lower horizontal parallel plates; the upper plate is marked B, and the lower plate is marked A; the charged small ball is located near point P between the two plates. The diagram only gives the relative positions of the plates and the position of point P, and does not show the situation of colliding with a plate. Then reason: take vertically upward as the positive direction. Plate A is below and plate B is above; when plate A is positively charged and the charge quantity of the capacitor is Q1, the electric field between the plates points from A to B, that is, upward. The small ball is just stationary at point P, indicating that the electric field force upward balances the gravity downward, therefore qE1=mg. For a parallel-plate capacitor, when the plate spacing is unchanged, the magnitude of the electric field strength is directly proportional to the charge quantity carried by the capacitor, so E2/E1=Q2/Q1. Let k=Q2/Q1. When the charge quantity suddenly increases to Q2 and plate A is still positively charged, the electric field is still upward, the resultant force is upward, and the small ball starts moving upward from rest at point P. The acceleration in this stage is a1=(qE2-mg)/m. From qE1=mg and E2=kE1, obtain qE2=kmg, so a1=g(k-1). After time t, make plate A negatively charged and plate B positively charged, and the magnitude of the charge quantity is still Q2. At this time the direction of the electric field reverses, and both the electric field force and gravity are downward, therefore the acceleration is a2=-(qE2+mg)/m=-g(k+1). During the first period of time t, the displacement is s1=(1/2)a1t^2, and the final velocity is v1=a1t. During the second period of time t, the displacement is s2=v1t+(1/2)a2t^2=a1t^2+(1/2)a2t^2. The problem states that after another time t the small ball just returns to point P, so the total displacement is zero: (1/2)a1t^2+a1t^2+(1/2)a2t^2=0. Simplifying gives 3a1+a2=0. Substitute a1=g(k-1), a2=-g(k+1): 3g(k-1)-g(k+1)=0, 3k-3-k-1=0, 2k-4=0, k=2. Therefore Q2/Q1=2, that is, Q2=2Q1. Final answer: Q2=2Q1.
